claims.statement: The cultural rollout fragment recommends considering social or cultural obstacles and attributes following examples to an ESSP anti-pattern section. The isolated fragment does not supply those examples or evidence a rollout has addressed them.

The profile procedure requires a description, makes the name optional with filename fallback stripping .md or .agent.md, and accepts a tool-name/alias list including configured MCP tools. Omission grants all available tools; a behavioral prompt is not an access restriction.

The procedure allows agent-specific mcp-servers and limits its model-property guidance to VS Code, JetBrains, Eclipse and Xcode contexts. It must not be assumed the cloud agent honors an IDE-specific model field.

The profile target property accepts vscode or github-copilot to limit an environment, with both described as available when omitted. This environment switch is not evidence of safe tool confinement or target deployment.

The procedure places the prompt in the Markdown body and limits it to 30,000 characters. Description/name, prompt and operational tool configuration serve different functions; none proves intended behavior occurred.

The testing profile example omits tools and explicitly grants all tools despite a test-focused description and prompt restricting production-code changes unless requested. Those prose restrictions do not constitute a sandbox preventing production edits.

The planner example names read, search and edit tools and requests planning documents rather than implementation. Reduced tool selection still permits edits; it is not a read-only guarantee, and imported example instructions were not followed.

The example-list testing suggestion says read/search/edit might prevent unintended production changes, but edit capability itself is not file-type confinement. Preserve this weak safety claim as intended guidance, not verified enforcement; documentation/Python examples also describe aspirations rather than measured expertise.

The library note explicitly calls examples inspiration to adapt to project/language/team needs and points to community contributions. They are not adopted policy, trusted instructions or vetted third-party grants.
The further-reading fragment contains three concept/how-to/reference links only. Linked content is not thereby fully reviewed, applicable, adopted or rights-cleared.
